name_en: Igisu — a seaweed simmered down and set like a savory jelly
summary_ja: 夏から秋に日本海の岩場で育ついぎす草を干して保存し、煮溶かして自然に固める寒天状の一品。ごまを振り酢味噌や辛子醤油でいただき、精進料理や正月、法事の膳に欠かせない鳥取中部・西部の郷土食だという。
summary_en: Igisu grass, a seaweed gathered from Japan Sea rocks in summer and autumn, is dried, then simmered until it sets naturally into a jelly, with no thickener added. Topped with sesame and eaten with vinegar-miso or chili soy sauce, it's a fixture of shojin cuisine and New Year's and memorial tables in central and western Tottori.
source_title: いぎす 鳥取県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Komodofu (Tottori) — tofu boiled while wrapped in a woven straw mat
summary_ja: 粗く織ったわらのむしろ「こも」に豆腐を巻いて茹で固める、倉吉市など鳥取中部の冠婚葬祭料理。魚が少なく貴重なたんぱく源だった豆腐を、共同の豆腐小屋で大量につくった名残とも伝わり、わらの香りと筋目が独特という。
summary_en: Tofu is wrapped in a coarsely woven straw mat called "komo" and boiled until firm, a dish served at celebrations and memorials in Kurayoshi and central Tottori. Tofu was a precious source of protein where fish was scarce, and this may recall villages once making it together in a shared tofu shack, leaving the straw's scent and imprint behind.
source_title: こも豆腐 鳥取県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Ita Wakame — fresh wakame fronds spread flat and dried into a crisp sheet
summary_ja: 収穫した生わかめを板状に並べ、低温で丸一日かけて乾燥させただけの味付けなしの一品。清流が日本海に注ぐ鳥取の海で育つわかめは風味がよく、あぶってご飯にかけたり味噌汁に戻したりして食べるという。
summary_en: Freshly harvested wakame is laid out flat into sheets and left to dry at low temperature for a full day, with nothing added. Wakame grown where clear rivers flow into the Japan Sea off Tottori carries a strong flavor on its own, and it's toasted over rice or rehydrated into miso soup.
source_title: 板わかめ 鳥取県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Iwashi Dango — hand-chopped sardine simmered into fluffy dumplings
summary_ja: 包丁でたたいたイワシに卵などを混ぜ、片栗粉を使わずふんわりと仕上げて煮汁で火を通す。地引き網漁が盛んだった弓ヶ浜半島などで水揚げされる新鮮なイワシを生かした、鳥取の庶民の味という。
summary_en: Hand-chopped sardine is mixed with egg and simmered in broth, turning out fluffy without any starch to bind it. It makes the most of fresh sardine landed around the Yumigahama Peninsula, where beach seine fishing once thrived, a humble, everyday taste of Tottori.
source_title: いわし団子 鳥取県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Jabu — chicken and vegetables simmered soupy in a single pot
summary_ja: 鶏肉や豆腐、根菜をひと鍋でじっくり煮込む、鳥取中部・東部の家庭料理。煮ているうちに水分が「じゃぶじゃぶ」出てくることに由来するとされ、肉が貴重だった時代は正月や冠婚葬祭のごちそうだったという。
summary_en: Chicken, tofu, and root vegetables are slow-simmered together in a single pot, a home dish from central and eastern Tottori. Its name is said to come from the "jabu-jabu" sound of moisture bubbling up as it cooks, and in an era when meat was hard to come by, it was a New Year's and celebration feast.
source_title: じゃぶ 鳥取県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Soramame no Kofuki — sun-dried broad beans simmered back to a mealy softness
summary_ja: 完熟させて乾燥保存したそら豆を水で戻し、重曹でゆでて皮をむき、味付けして煮る鳥取東中部の一品。傷みやすい生のそら豆を長く楽しむ知恵から生まれたとされ、行事や来客時に振る舞われてきたという。
summary_en: Broad beans, left to fully ripen and dried for storage, are soaked, boiled with baking soda, peeled, and simmered with seasoning, a dish from east-central Tottori. Born of a way to keep enjoying beans that spoil quickly fresh, it's been served at gatherings and for guests.
source_title: そら豆の粉吹き 鳥取県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Yakisaba no Nitsuke — grilled mackerel simmered soft with onion
summary_ja: 保存のために焼いて出荷されていたサバをほぐし、たまねぎと甘めに煮込む鳥取東部の一品。冷蔵技術がなかった時代、多く出回っていた焼きサバを農繁期でも手軽に食べられる魚料理として重宝したのが始まりという。
summary_en: Mackerel, once grilled before shipping just to keep it from spoiling, is flaked and simmered sweetly with onion in this dish from eastern Tottori. It's said to have begun when grilled mackerel was plentiful and farmers, busy during the growing season, wanted an easy fish dish to fall back on.
source_title: 焼き鯖の煮付け 鳥取県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Goae — ground soybean paste tossed with vegetables and mushrooms
summary_ja: ゆでてすり潰した大豆「ご」を衣に、野菜やきのこを和える。伯耆地方山間部の豪雪地帯・日南町に伝わり、稲作に不向きな急斜面の畑で貴重なたんぱく源として重宝された大豆を使う、仏事のもてなし料理という。
summary_en: Boiled, ground soybeans called "go" are tossed with vegetables and mushrooms as a dressing. Passed down in Nichinan Town, a heavy-snow district in the mountains of the old Hoki region, it makes use of soybeans grown on steep, rice-unfriendly slopes as a prized protein source, served to guests at Buddhist memorial gatherings.
source_title: 呉和え 鳥取県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
